newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Narrow slightly to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Narrow slightly to U.S..

text.p: Australian bond yield spreads narrowed slightly against U.S. debt after Thursday's sharp blow out following a stronger than expected wages reported amid some covering ahead of U.S. non-farm payrolls later on Friday.

Despite this narrowing the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread was still way above the sub-100 basis points seen at the end of last week, and this week's underperformance was even more notable at the short end as easing expectations faded.
The three-year spread between the two was below 20 basis points last Friday.
Friday's slightly weaker than expected outcome to local March and quarterly retail trade failed to make much impression with the focus now squarely on the U.S.
April payrolls are forecast to 211,000 after 175,000 in March, while the unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 5.2 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

Elsewhere, Canadian bonds continued their outperformance of the U.S. of the past few days, helped by a stronger Canadian dollar after the recent U.S. data flow suggested that a May tightening by the Federal Reserve was not a foregone conclusion, relieving pressure on Canadian policy.
Australian debt put in a mild outperformance against New Zealand, despite aggressive buying of N.Z. debt.
